{{short description|2019–20 New Mexico lobos men's basketball team}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox college sports team season |year=2020–21 |team=New Mexico Lobos |sport=Basketball |image=New Mexico Lobos wordmark.svg |image_size=250 |conference=Mountain West Conference |short_conf=MW |record= 6–16 |conf_record= 2–15 |head_coach= [[Paul Weir (basketball)|Paul Weir]] |hc_year = 4th |asst_coach1= Dan McHale |asst_coach2= [[Scott Padgett]] |asst_coach3= Ralph Davis |stadium= |champion= |tourney= |tourney_result= }} {{2020–21 Mountain West Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2020–21 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of New Mexico]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Lobos were led by fourth-year head coach [[Paul Weir (basketball)|Paul Weir]] and are members of the [[Mountain West Conference]]. Due to [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19]] restrictions within the state of [[New Mexico]], the Lobos did not play any of their home games at their normal home arena [[The Pit (arena)|The Pit]].{{Cite web|last=Schrotenboer|first=Brent|date=November 25, 2020|title=Should New Mexico's college teams be crossing state lines to avoid pandemic restrictions?|url=http://usatoday.com/story/sports/2020/11/25/new-mexico-college-teams-flee-state-avoid-rules-raising-issues/6414132002/|url-status=live|access-date=May 3, 2021|website=USA Today|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201125175027/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/2020/11/25/new-mexico-college-teams-flee-state-avoid-rules-raising-issues/6414132002/ |archive-date=2020-11-25 }}{{Cite web|last=Rosenzweig-Ziff|first=Dan|date=2020-11-20|title=Fleeing their home state's strict restrictions on sports, New Mexico basketball teams seek refuge in two of Texas' worst hot spots|url=https://www.texastribune.org/2020/11/19/new-mexico-basketball-texas-lubbock-coronavirus/|access-date=2021-05-03|website=The Texas Tribune|language=en}} Their "home" games were played at various different locations outside of the state of New Mexico. They finished the season 6–16, with a 2–15 record in [[2020–21 Mountain West Conference basketball season|Mountain West]] play, finishing in last place in the conference. As the No. 11 seed in the [[2021 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|Mountain West tournament]], they lost in the first round to [[2020–21 Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Fresno State]] 85–77. Prior to the end of the season, the school announced that Weir would not return as head coach.{{Cite web|date=2021-02-27|title=Weir out as New Mexico coach at end of season|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30971404/paul-weir-new-mexico-lobos-men-basketball-coach-end-season|access-date=2021-05-03|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} On March 16, the school named former [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] head coach [[Richard Pitino]] the team's new head coach.{{Cite web|title=New Mexico hires Richard Pitino as next coach less than 24 hours after Minnesota firing|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/new-mexico-hires-richard-pitino-as-next-coach-less-than-24-hours-after-minnesota-firing/|access-date=2021-05-03|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}} == Previous season == The [[2019–20 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team|Lobos]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 19–14, 7–11 in [[2019–20 Mountain West Conference men's basketball season|Mountain West play]] to finish in a tie for seventh place. They defeated [[2019–20 San Jose State Spartans basketball team|San Jose State]] in the first round of the [[2020 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|Mountain West tournament]] before losing in the quarterfinals to [[2019–20 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team|Utah State]]. == Roster == {{CBB roster/Header|year=2020|team=New Mexico Lobos|teamcolors=y|high_school=yes}} {{CBB roster/Player|first=Isaiah|last=Marin|num=0|pos=G|ft=6|in=5|lbs=190|class=fr|rs=y|home=[[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix, AZ]]|high_school=[[Buckeye Union High School|Buckeye Union HS]]}} {{CBB roster/Player|first=Bayron|last=Matos|num=1|pos=F|ft=6|in=9|lbs=215|class=fr|rs=y|home=[[Santo Domingo]], [[Dominican Republic]]|high_school=Hamilton Heights Christian Academy}} {{CBB roster/Player|first=Saquan|last=Singleton|num=2|pos=G|ft=6|in=6|lbs=190|class=jr|rs=|home=[[The Bronx|Bronx, NY]]|high_school=[[Monsignor Scanlan High School|Monsignor Scanlan HS]]
